value.name: SPOAN
value.display_name: Spastic paraplegia, optic atrophy and neuropathy (KLC2)

subtype_term.preferred_term: spastic paraplegia, optic atropy, and neuropathy

term.label: spastic paraplegia, optic atropy, and neuropathy

value.description: SPOAN syndrome, caused by a homozygous 216-bp deletion in the non-coding region upstream of KLC2 that leads to KLC2 overexpression - a recessive disease mechanism acting through increased rather than lost gene product. KLC2 is a kinesin light chain, which is why it is bound on the kinesin-dependent axonal cargo transport node. ClinGen has no KLC2 gene-disease validity record. Note that the bound MONDO label carries the misspelling 'optic atropy'; it is copied here as the ontology's canonical label.

selected_evidence.snippet: SPOAN syndrome is a neurodegenerative disorder mainly characterized by spastic paraplegia, optic atrophy and neuropathy (SPOAN).

value.name: SPG74
value.description: SPG74, caused by a homozygous IBA57 donor splice-site mutation in a highly consanguineous family whose ten affected members had a childhood-onset SPOAN-like phenotype - spastic paraplegia with optic atrophy and peripheral neuropathy - progressing slowly into late adulthood. IBA57 is a mitochondrial iron-sulfur protein assembly factor, which is why it is bound on the mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly node. ClinGen curates IBA57 against mitochondrial disease (Definitive) rather than against an HSP entity.

assertion.name: IBA57
assertion.notes: The committed ClinGen snapshot curates IBA57 against mitochondrial disease (MONDO:0044970, Definitive, autosomal recessive) rather than against an HSP entity.

selected_evidence.snippet: We mapped this disorder to a locus on chromosome 1q and identified a homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the IBA57 gene

value.name: SPG54
value.description: SPG54, caused by recessive DDHD2 variants in four families. The defining report gives the core phenotype as very early-onset spastic paraplegia with intellectual disability and a specific pattern of brain abnormalities on imaging, and reports an abnormal lipid peak on cerebral magnetic resonance spectroscopy as a distinguishing biomarker. DDHD2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase A1, which is why it is bound on the membrane-lipid node. ClinGen has no DDHD2 gene-disease validity record.

selected_evidence.snippet: The core phenotype of this HSP syndrome consists of very early-onset (<2 years) spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability, and a specific pattern of brain abnormalities on cerebral imaging.

value.name: SPG70
value.description: SPG70, attributed to MARS1 (methionyl-tRNA synthetase 1). This is the most thinly evidenced row on the entry: a PubMed search for the SPG70 designation and for MARS1/MARS together with spastic paraplegia returned no dedicated SPG70 report, and the human evidence cited here is a childhood-onset HSP case series in which MARS was the confirmed genetic etiology in two of sixteen patients. ClinGen has not curated MARS1 against any HSP entity; its only MARS1 record is Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Limited, autosomal dominant). The autosomal recessive designation follows the bound MONDO class label.

assertion.name: MARS1
assertion.notes: PubMed searches run 2026-09-26 for the SPG70 designation ("spastic paraplegia 70", SPG70 hereditary spastic paraplegia) and for MARS1 or MARS together with spastic paraplegia returned no dedicated SPG70 report, so the human evidence cited here is a childhood-onset HSP case series in which MARS was the confirmed genetic etiology in two of sixteen patients. The committed ClinGen gene-validity snapshot holds one MARS1 record, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Limited, autosomal dominant), and none against an HSP entity. The autosomal recessive mode recorded here follows the bound MONDO class label rather than a cited study.

selected_evidence.snippet: Genetically confirmed etiologies included SPAST (3 patients), MARS (2), KIF1A (2), KIF5A (1), SACS (1), SPG7 (1), REEP1 (1), PNPT1 (1), MT-ATP6 (1), and ATL1 (1).

value.name: SPG15
value.description: SPG15, caused by biallelic truncating ZFYVE26 (spastizin) variants; six different truncating mutations segregated with disease in eight families whose phenotype included variable features of Kjellin syndrome. Spastizin colocalizes partially with endoplasmic reticulum and endosomal markers, which is why ZFYVE26 is also bound on the endolysosomal and ESCRT membrane-traffic node. The ZFYVE26 record in `genetic` points at this row. ClinGen has no ZFYVE26 gene-disease validity record.

value.name: SPG39
value.description: SPG39, the spastic-paraplegia presentation of the PNPLA6 disorder spectrum, which also includes Gordon-Holmes, Boucher-Neuhauser, Oliver-McFarlane and Laurence-Moon syndromes. dismech curates the ataxia-hypogonadism-choroidal dystrophy end of that spectrum separately as Boucher-Neuhauser_Syndrome; this row carries the spastic-paraplegia end. ClinGen's Definitive PNPLA6 record for spastic paraplegia is filed against its own entity (PNPLA6-related spastic paraplegia with or without ataxia, MONDO:0100149) rather than against the SPG39 class bound here.

assertion.name: PNPLA6
assertion.notes: ClinGen files its Definitive PNPLA6 spastic-paraplegia record against its own entity, PNPLA6-related spastic paraplegia with or without ataxia (MONDO:0100149), rather than against the SPG39 class bound on this subtype; its second PNPLA6 record is the retinal dystrophy-ataxia-pituitary hormone abnormality-hypogonadism syndrome (MONDO:0100155), whose Boucher-Neuhauser presentation is a separate dismech entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: A wide spectrum of neurodegenerative diseases has been associated with pathogenic variants in the PNPLA6 (patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 6) gene, including spastic paraplegia type 39, Gordon-Holmes, Boucher-Neuhauser, Oliver-Mc Farlane, and Laurence-Moon syndromes.

value.name: SPG43
value.description: SPG43, caused by a homozygous C19orf12 missense variant first reported in two Malian sisters. C19orf12 is allelic with neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation, which dismech curates in Neurodegeneration_With_Brain_Iron_Accumulation; the two presentations are distinguished in the defining report by brain imaging, which showed no iron deposition in the SPG43 subjects. ClinGen's only C19orf12 records are for neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 4.

assertion.name: C19orf12
assertion.notes: Allelic with neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation, curated in dismech as Neurodegeneration_With_Brain_Iron_Accumulation; the committed ClinGen snapshot holds two C19orf12 records, both against neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 4 (MONDO:0013674), and none against SPG43.

selected_evidence.snippet: We report here the genetic basis for a form of progressive hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG43) previously described in two Malian sisters. Exome sequencing revealed a homozygous missense variant (c.187G>C; p.Ala63Pro) in C19orf12

value.name: SPG85
value.description: SPG85, caused by bi-allelic RNF170 variants in four unrelated families. RNF170 is the ubiquitin E3 ligase that targets inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors for degradation, which is why it is bound on the endoplasmic reticulum calcium-release node alongside ERLIN2. The dominant RNF170 disease at the other end of the same allelic series, autosomal dominant sensory ataxia 1, is curated separately as Autosomal_Dominant_Sensory_Ataxia_1, which already records SPG85 as a differential diagnosis. ClinGen has no RNF170 gene-disease validity record.

assertion.name: RNF170
assertion.notes: The dominant disease at the other end of the same RNF170 allelic series, autosomal dominant sensory ataxia 1 (MONDO:0012166), is a separate dismech entry which already records SPG85 as a differential diagnosis rather than as one of its own manifestations.

selected_evidence.snippet: We provide evidence that mutations in the ubiquitin E3 ligase gene RNF170, which targets inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors for degradation, are the likely cause of autosomal recessive HSP in four unrelated families

value.name: SPG57
value.description: SPG57, caused by homozygous TFG variants. Two consanguineous Iranian families carrying homozygous TFG missense variants were reported with early-onset progressive muscle weakness, spasticity and further neurological features. ClinGen has no TFG gene-disease validity record.

selected_evidence.snippet: the tropomyosin-receptor kinase fused gene (TFG) has been linked to diverse hereditary neurodegenerative disorders, including a very rare complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, named spastic paraplegia type 57 (SPG57)

value.name: DEE113
value.description: SV2A encodes synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A, the binding site of levetiracetam. The reported lesion is a homozygous R383Q missense change in a multiply consanguineous family: the proband had intractable epilepsy, involuntary movements, microcephaly and developmental and growth retardation, and an earlier-born brother had a similar course and died at 7 months of age. Levetiracetam was not effective in the proband. The evidence base for this subtype is thin - a single family, with no independent replication found in a PubMed search on 2026-09-25 using the queries 'SV2A biallelic variants developmental and epileptic encephalopathy' (no hits), 'SV2A gene variants patients epilepsy developmental delay cohort' (no hits) and 'synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A SV2A homozygous variant patients' (this report only).

assertion.notes: Synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A and the binding site of levetiracetam. A single homozygous R383Q missense variant in one consanguineous family is the whole reported basis of this subtype; levetiracetam was ineffective in the proband.

value.name: DKCA6
value.display_name: Dyskeratosis congenita, autosomal dominant 6 (ACD/TPP1 TEL patch)
value.description: The numbered, autosomal dominant designation for ACD/TPP1 telomere biology disease (OMIM 616553). It sits inside the gene-level ACD subtype above, which spans both dominant and recessive ACD disease; DKCA6 names the dominant half. The defining report is a family in which a single-amino-acid deletion in the TPP1 TEL patch, p.Lys170del, segregates with aplastic anaemia and related haematopoietic disease, and in which every carrier, but no wild-type relative, has short telomeres. The molecular lesion is specifically a telomerase-recruitment defect rather than a loss of telomere binding: expressed in 293T cells the mutant protein still reaches telomeres but no longer brings telomerase with it. Presentation in that family was led by bone marrow failure rather than by the classic mucocutaneous triad; how far that generalises is not established, since the dominant ACD allelic series is still small.

The lesion is a telomerase-recruitment defect rather than a loss of telomere binding: the mutant protein still localises to telomeres but no longer brings telomerase with it. The Genetic class carries no slot for that distinction, so it is recorded here.

selected_evidence.snippet: When introduced into 293T cells, TPP1 with the ΔK170 mutation is able to localize to telomeres but fails to recruit telomerase to telomeres, supporting a causal relationship between this TPP1 mutation and bone marrow disorders.

value.description: The adult, pulmonary-fibrosis-predominant POT1 presentation, and the eighth locus of the numbered telomere-related pulmonary fibrosis / bone marrow failure series. It is defined by a Dutch family carrying the heterozygous POT1 p.(L259S) allele in which idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis segregates dominantly with short leukocyte telomeres and genetic anticipation. This is the same shelterin gene as the recessive POT1 subtype above but a different clinical entity: dominant rather than recessive, adult rather than childhood, and led by lung disease rather than by the mucocutaneous triad. Mechanistically L259S is not a simple null - the mutant protein fails to bind the telomeric overhang, to accumulate in the nucleus, to regulate telomerase negatively and to support lagging-strand maintenance, and patient cells show telomere loss, telomere-induced DNA damage and premature senescence with G1 arrest. The evidence base is one family plus functional characterisation, so the phenotypic boundaries of this subtype remain provisional.

variants.name: STUB1 p.Glu28Lys
variants.description: TPR-domain disease-associated allele. Recombinant Hsc70- and self-ubiquitination were similar to wild type in 2017, with altered proteolytic susceptibility and oligomer distribution.

variants.name: STUB1 p.Asn65Ser
variants.description: TPR-domain disease-associated allele with impaired Hsc70 ubiquitination but preserved self-ubiquitination, increased dimerization and resistance to limited proteolysis in 2017.

variants.name: STUB1 p.Lys145Gln
variants.description: Disease-associated allele with wild-type-like ubiquitination in the 2017 recombinant assays and altered protein structural properties; cellular and other-substrate effects require separate evidence.

variants.name: STUB1 p.Ser236Thr
variants.description: Disease-associated allele with wild-type-like Hsc70- and self-ubiquitination in 2017 but altered structural stability. The 2013 HEK293 NR2A-degradation assay showed a defect, illustrating substrate- and context-dependent functional results.

variants.name: STUB1 p.Thr246Met

variants.name: STUB1 c.430A>T (p.Lys144Ter)

variants.name: STUB1 c.355C>T (p.Arg119Ter)

variants.name: STUB1 c.880A>T (p.Ile294Phe)

variants.name: STUB1 c.728C>T (p.Pro243Leu)
variants.description: U-box variant confirmed in trans with p.Lys145Gln in two siblings with ataxia, severe cognitive decline, spasticity and choreoathetosis.

variants.name: STUB1 NM_005861.2:c.612+11C>G
variants.description: Maternally inherited homozygous intronic variant in a patient with Gordon Holmes features and chromosome-16 regions of absent heterozygosity consistent with maternal uniparental isodisomy. The 2024 online report classified the variant as uncertain despite considering the presentation diagnostic. SpliceAI and MaxEntScan predicted donor-site gain; no patient RNA or functional splice assay was reported. The case was investigated through the observational HSP Genomic Sequencing Initiative (NCT05354622); study ascertainment does not establish this variant as causal.

variants.name: STUB1 NM_005861.4:c.352C>T (p.Gln118Ter)

value.description: Autosomal dominant axonal CMT caused by JAG1 variants, distinguished by severe vocal fold paresis from recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement. assertion.notes: Autosomal dominant JAG1 missense variants cause axonal CMT2 with severe vocal fold paresis. JAG1 is far better known as the Alagille syndrome gene, and the only JAG1 row in the ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity CSV (snapshot 2026-08-13) is Definitive for Alagille syndrome due to a JAG1 point mutation; that CSV carries no JAG1 row for any neuropathy concept. selected_evidence.snippet: Affected individuals in both families exhibited severe vocal fold paresis, a rare feature of peripheral nerve disease that can be life-threatening.

value.name: CMT2FF
value.description: Autosomal dominant axonal CMT with marked upper limb involvement, caused by the recurrent CADM3 p.Tyr172Cys variant. CADM3 is the axonal partner of Schwann-cell CADM4 at the axon-glia interface.

assertion.name: CADM3 (CMT2FF)
assertion.notes: A single recurrent CADM3 variant, Tyr172Cys, was found in three unrelated families including one de novo case, and is absent from 230,000 control chromosomes in gnomAD. CADM3 is the axonal member of the CADM adhesion pair that organizes the myelinated fibre with Schwann-cell CADM4. Inheritance is autosomal dominant. A search of the approved symbol CADM3 in the ClinGen Gene-Disease Validity CSV (snapshot 2026-08-13) returns no row, so no expert panel has yet classified this relationship.

selected_evidence.snippet: Most CADM3 patients share a similar phenotype consisting of autosomal dominant CMT2 with marked upper limb involvement.

value.name: CMT2V
value.description: Dominantly inherited late-onset neuropathy attributed to heterozygous NAGLU variants in two families. In the large French-Canadian family the allele is the missense p.Ile403Thr, the presentation is painful and sensory-predominant, and carriers show a mean 45% decrease in alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase activity. A second, North-American family was found through a CMT2 patient and carries a nonsense allele, p.Glu123X, segregating in all three available affected members, who had mild muscular weakness and diminished reflexes alongside sensory loss and pain; no enzyme assay was done in that family. Biallelic NAGLU loss causes mucopolysaccharidosis IIIB instead.

assertion.name: NAGLU
assertion.notes: Lysosomal alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase. The CMT2V claim rests on two families in the defining report: a large French-Canadian family in which the heterozygous missense allele p.Ile403Thr segregates with a late-onset painful sensory-predominant neuropathy and carriers show a mean 45% decrease in enzyme activity, and a North-American family carrying the nonsense allele p.Glu123X, in which affected members also had mild muscular weakness and diminished reflexes. Biallelic loss causes mucopolysaccharidosis IIIB instead. No enzyme assay was performed in the second family, and how a partial enzyme deficiency produces the neuropathy is not established in nerve, so no mechanism edge to axonal degeneration is asserted for this gene.

selected_evidence.snippet: No enzymatic assay was performed on Family 2.

value.description: The non-syndromic end of the ARX allelic series. ARX encodes an Aristaless-related homeobox transcription factor expressed specifically in telencephalon and ventral thalamus. assertion.notes: Aristaless-related homeobox transcription factor with telencephalon- and ventral-thalamus-restricted expression. Polyalanine expansions and certain missense alleles give the non-syndromic phenotype modelled here; other alleles in the same gene cause distinct syndromic entities.

selected_evidence.snippet: In contrast to other genes involved in XLMR, ARX expression is specific to the telencephalon and ventral thalamus.

value.name: MRX105
value.description: USP27X, encoding ubiquitin-specific peptidase 27, was identified in the same X-exome screen of 405 unresolved families as KLHL15 and FRMPD4, with a second unrelated family carrying a missense variant substituting a highly conserved tryptophan. The gene's function in neurons is largely uncharacterised - its only known interaction partner is USP22, required for glial and neuronal development in flies - so this subtype currently has a gene assignment without a worked-out mechanism, and the entry wires it to the class's shared convergent node rather than to a specific pathway. The ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel classifies USP27X as Moderate against "X-linked complex neurodevelopmental disorder".

assertion.name: USP27X
assertion.notes: Ubiquitin specific peptidase 27 X-linked. Identified by X-exome sequencing of 405 unresolved families, with a second unrelated family carrying a conserved-residue missense variant. selected_evidence.snippet: Little is currently known about the functional role of the ubiquitin specific peptidase USP27X.

value.name: MRX90
value.description: Truncating variants in DLG3, which encodes synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), found in 4 of 329 families screened for moderate to severe X-linked intellectual disability - among the higher per-gene yields in the class. SAP102 is a membrane-associated guanylate kinase localised to the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses, whose PDZ domains bind the NR2 subunits of the NMDA receptor. Every reported allele truncates within or before the third PDZ domain, so the proposed mechanism is loss of NMDA receptor targeting and downstream signalling, which is the most direct molecular route to the impaired synaptic plasticity this entry models as the shared endpoint. Together with SYP this is one of only two genes in the whole checklist that the ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates against this entry's own MONDO term rather than against a broader neurodevelopmental anchor, and it holds the Definitive classification.

assertion.name: DLG3
assertion.notes: Discs large MAGUK scaffold protein 3, encoding synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), a membrane-associated guanylate kinase of the postsynaptic density of excitatory synapses whose PDZ domains bind the NR2 subunits of the NMDA receptor. selected_evidence.snippet: DLG3 encodes synapse-associated protein 102 (SAP102), a member of the membrane-associated guanylate kinase protein family.

value.name: MRX103
value.description: KLHL15 was one of seven novel and validated X-linked intellectual disability genes identified by X-exome sequencing of 405 unresolved families - the study that also delivered FRMPD4 and USP27X in this entry. A protein-truncating variant was found in a large family, with further support from an unrelated family carrying a partial KLHL15 deletion. KLHL15 is a kelch-like protein that acts as a substrate adaptor for Cul3-based E3 ubiquitin ligases, targeting a brain-specific regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A for proteasomal degradation, so like MID2 and USP27X it belongs to the ubiquitin-proteasome theme. The phenotype is not uniformly pure: the same report notes a KLHL15 partial deletion described in a proband with severe intellectual disability, epilepsy and cortical developmental anomalies, and KLHL15 has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

assertion.name: KLHL15
assertion.notes: Kelch-like family member 15, a substrate adaptor for Cul3-based E3 ubiquitin ligases that targets a brain-specific regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A for proteasomal degradation. No ClinGen gene-disease validity curation exists for this gene.

selected_evidence.snippet: KLHL15-Cul3 specifically targets a brain-specific regulatory subunit of the protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A/B'ß) and thereby promotes its proteasomal degradation, resulting in the formation of alternative PP2A holoenzymes.

value.name: MRX96
value.description: SYP, encoding synaptophysin, was one of nine genes implicated in X-linked intellectual disability by the systematic resequencing of X-chromosome coding exons in 208 families. Synaptophysin is an integral synaptic vesicle protein accounting for roughly a tenth of total synaptic vesicle protein cargo; four separate SYP variants were found in affected families. Functional follow-up in synaptophysin-knockout mouse neurons showed that the patient variants fail to support efficient retrieval of synaptobrevin II, giving this subtype a defined lesion in the synaptic vesicle cycle. The ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates SYP against this entry's own MONDO term and classifies the relationship as Moderate, so the gene assignment is supported but not yet definitive.

assertion.name: SYP
assertion.notes: Synaptophysin, an integral synaptic vesicle protein that accounts for about a tenth of total synaptic vesicle protein cargo and is required for efficient retrieval of synaptobrevin II from the plasma membrane during endocytosis. Patient variants either mislocalise throughout the axon or reach the nerve terminal without supporting that retrieval.

selected_evidence.snippet: The screen has discovered nine genes implicated in XLMR, including SYP, ZNF711 and CASK reported here, confirming the power of this strategy.

value.name: MRX72
value.description: Null alleles of RAB39B, a neuronal-specific small GTPase of the Golgi compartment, identified in two male patients - one of them in the MRX72 family, where a 5' splice-site change abolished normal splicing. Its downregulation alters neurite growth cone number and morphology and reduces presynaptic boutons, placing the subtype in the vesicular trafficking theme. Intellectual disability was accompanied by autism spectrum disorder, epileptic seizures and macrocephaly in some, not all, affected family members, which is the variable-comorbidity pattern this class tolerates rather than a reproducible syndromic signature. The row carries a live caveat: the ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates RAB39B as Definitive against an early-onset parkinsonism-intellectual disability syndrome (MONDO:0010709), a separate MONDO term with no dismech entry, rather than against this one. Parkinsonism is not reported in the founding MRX72 publication, so the two entities are separated here by phenotype and age of onset rather than by allele, and this row should not be read as covering the parkinsonism entity.

assertion.name: RAB39B
assertion.notes: A neuronal-specific small GTPase of the RAB family localised to the Golgi compartment. Null alleles - a near-start stop codon in one family and a 5' splice-site change in the MRX72 family - produce no protein, and downregulation reduces presynaptic boutons and disturbs neurite growth cones. The same gene is curated by ClinGen against an early-onset parkinsonism-intellectual disability syndrome (MONDO:0010709), a separate entity that is not curated here.

selected_evidence.snippet: We show that RAB39B, a novel RAB GTPase of unknown function, is a neuronal-specific protein that is localized to the Golgi compartment.

value.name: MRX101
value.description: A missense variant in MID2, encoding an E3 ubiquitin ligase, reported as the likely cause of X-linked intellectual disability in one large Indian kindred, where it was present in all affected males and obligate carriers and absent from unaffected males and from 200 population controls. The variant abolishes the function of the protein's COS domain, and the mutant protein accumulates in the cytoplasm instead of binding the cytoskeleton. This row rests on a single large pedigree plus one further variant found by screening 480 unrelated individuals, and MID2 has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation, so the assignment is thinner than most in this entry and is recorded with that caveat. It is the ubiquitin-pathway theme's entry point in the class, and the authors emphasise that the MID2 phenotype differs from that reported for its paralogue MID1.

assertion.name: MID2
assertion.notes: Midline 2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase. The reported causal allele abolishes the function of the protein's COS domain, and the mutant protein accumulates in the cytoplasm instead of binding the cytoskeleton. The assignment rests on a single large kindred plus one further variant from a 480-individual screen, and has no ClinGen gene-disease validity curation.

selected_evidence.snippet: When transiently expressed in HEK293T cell line, the mutation was found to abolish the function of the COS domain in the protein.

value.name: MRX104
value.description: Deleterious FRMPD4 variants - an exon deletion, a nonsense change, a frameshift and a conserved-residue missense - in ten affected males from four unrelated families. FRMPD4 is a neural scaffolding protein that binds PSD-95 to promote dendritic spine morphogenesis and regulates mGluR1/5 signalling through Homer, so this subtype sits at the postsynaptic scaffold alongside DLG3. The frameshift allele disrupts binding to both PSD-95 and HOMER1 and fails to increase spine density in transfected hippocampal neurons, and knockout mice show hippocampus-dependent spatial learning deficits. Two qualifications belong on this row: the reporting authors describe the entity as a new X-linked intellectual disability syndrome, with language delay, seizures and behavioural or psychiatric disturbance alongside moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, and the ClinGen Intellectual Disability and Autism Gene Curation Expert Panel curates FRMPD4 as Definitive against "X-linked complex neurodevelopmental disorder" rather than against this class. OMIM and MONDO nonetheless number the entity within the non-syndromic series, and it is recorded here on that basis with the comorbidity stated rather than suppressed. A third point matters for the evidence audit this entry runs on itself: of the fourteen genes admitted in this enumeration pass, FRMPD4 is the only one named in either list that the 2013 reassessment against 10,563 control X chromosomes singles out, and it falls in the fifteen for which replication studies were warranted rather than in the ten whose involvement was questioned. Both reports cited on this row postdate that flag and supply the independent families it asked for.

assertion.name: FRMPD4
assertion.notes: FERM and PDZ domain containing 4, a neural scaffolding protein that interacts with PSD-95 to promote dendritic spine morphogenesis and with mGluR1/5 and Homer to regulate mGluR1/5 signalling. selected_evidence.snippet: FRMPD4 (FERM and PDZ Domain Containing 4) is a neural scaffolding protein that interacts with PSD-95 to positively regulate dendritic spine morphogenesis, and with mGluR1/5 and Homer to regulate mGluR1/5 signaling.

value.description: ZNF711 was implicated by the same 208-family X-chromosome resequencing screen that reported SYP, and was subsequently confirmed in two large four-generation pedigrees with eleven affected males, bringing the total to four families. value.name: NPPA-related
value.description: Familial AF linked to variants in NPPA, encoding the atrial natriuretic peptide precursor. The mechanism is not a channel defect: a frameshift produces a circulating chimeric peptide, and the proposal is that this peptide, rather than loss of the normal one, shortens the atrial action potential. The circulating peptide is documented in human carriers, but the shortening step is shown in isolated perfused rat heart rather than in human atrium, so the peptide-to-substrate link remains an inference from a model system.

assertion.name: NPPA variants
assertion.features: Variants in NPPA (atrial natriuretic peptide precursor) are linked to familial AF.
assertion.notes: NPPA is the one locus in this entry whose product is a circulating hormone rather than an ion channel or a junctional protein. The defining family was mapped by linkage to 1p36-p35 and carries a heterozygous frameshift; the mutant peptide circulates at high concentration and shortens the atrial action potential, which is how the entry connects it to the shared re-entry-prone substrate.

selected_evidence.snippet: shortened atrial action potentials were seen in an isolated heart model, creating a possible substrate for atrial fibrillation

value.name: KCNE2-related
value.description: Familial AF associated with gain-of-function variants in the potassium-channel beta subunit KCNE2, which modulates KCNQ1 and other cardiac potassium currents.

assertion.name: KCNE2 gain-of-function variants
assertion.features: Gain-of-function variants in the potassium-channel beta subunit KCNE2 are associated with familial AF through enhancement of cardiac potassium current.
assertion.notes: The reported lesion is a single recurrent substitution, R27C, found in 2 of 28 unrelated Chinese AF kindreds, cosegregating with disease in both and absent from 462 controls. Its functional effect parallels KCNQ1 S140G - a gain of function on the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel - which is why the two are modelled on the same repolarization-shortening arm of this entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: Similar to KCNQ1 S140G, the mutation had a gain-of-function effect on the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel; unlike long QT syndrome-associated KCNE2 mutations, it did not alter HERG-KCNE2 current.

value.name: SCN1B-related
value.display_name: SCN1B sodium channel beta-1 familial AF
value.description: AF associated with variants in SCN1B, encoding the sodium channel beta-1 subunit, which modulates Nav1.5 gating kinetics and membrane expression. The reported variants reduce SCN5A-mediated current, placing this subtype with the reduced-sodium-current arm rather than the repolarization arm. The index report is a case-control screen of 480 AF patients rather than a pedigree study, so these are susceptibility variants absent from controls rather than demonstrated Mendelian segregation.

assertion.name: SCN1B loss-of-function variants
assertion.association: Reported in AF probands without family segregation
assertion.features: Two nonsynonymous variants, R85H and D153N, identified in AF probands and absent from controls; both reduce SCN5A-mediated current when coexpressed.
assertion.notes:
SCN1B and SCN2B were reported together in one screen of 480 AF patients against 548 controls. The variants are rare, at conserved residues, absent from controls, and reduce sodium current in heterologous expression - but the report describes probands rather than pedigrees, so cosegregation is not established and the grading here is UNKNOWN.
A detail worth carrying: three of the four beta-subunit variant carriers had saddleback right-precordial ST elevation, which places these variants in the Brugada-overlap part of the sodium-channel spectrum rather than in isolated AF.

selected_evidence.snippet: In 3 of 4 mutation carriers, the ECGs showed saddleback-type ST-segment elevation in the right precordial leads.

value.name: KCNA5-related
value.description: Familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in KCNA5, encoding the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.5 (ultra-rapid delayed rectifier current, IKur), which is predominantly expressed in atrial cardiomyocytes. Loss of IKur prolongs atrial action potential duration and may predispose to early afterdepolarizations and AF. This subtype runs the entry's main mechanism backwards: the potassium-channel arm shortens the atrial action potential and this one lengthens it, so a shortened refractory period is not a necessary condition for familial AF.

assertion.name: KCNA5 loss-of-function variants
assertion.features: A heterozygous nonsense variant, E375X, truncates Kv1.5 before the voltage sensor and pore, abolishing the atrial-selective ultrarapid delayed rectifier current IKur and acting dominant-negatively on the wild-type channel.
assertion.notes:
KCNA5 runs opposite to the potassium-channel subtypes above: KCNQ1, KCNE2 and KCNJ2 act by gain of function and shorten the atrial action potential, whereas KCNA5 loss of IKur prolongs it and produces early afterdepolarization and triggered activity. Both routes converge on an arrhythmogenic atrium, which is worth keeping visible because it means action potential shortening is not a necessary feature of monogenic AF.
The channel is described by its discoverers as expressed in human atria, which is the reason a defect in it produces an atrial arrhythmia.

selected_evidence.snippet: Loss of channel function translated into action potential prolongation and early after-depolarization in human atrial myocytes, increasing vulnerability to stress-provoked triggered activity.

value.name: SCN5A-related
value.description: Familial AF associated with variants in the cardiac sodium channel SCN5A, overlapping the broader SCN5A-related arrhythmia spectrum.

assertion.name: SCN5A variants
assertion.features: Cardiac sodium-channel SCN5A variants are associated with familial AF as part of the broader SCN5A arrhythmia spectrum.
assertion.notes: Graded RISK_FACTOR rather than CAUSATIVE deliberately. The largest resequencing study found novel variants in 2.7% of AF probands with cosegregation in six informative families, but its own conclusion is that such variants "may predispose" to AF, and a further 3.2% of probands carried rare variants already attributed to long-QT or Brugada syndrome. SCN5A is therefore better read as a shared arrhythmia-susceptibility locus whose AF phenotype overlaps other sodium-channel syndromes than as a dedicated familial-AF gene.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mutations or rare variants in SCN5A may predispose patients with or without underlying heart disease to AF.

value.name: KCNJ2-related
value.description: Autosomal dominant familial AF caused by gain-of-function KCNJ2 variants (e.g. V93I) that increase the inward-rectifier IK1 current.

assertion.name: KCNJ2 gain-of-function variants
assertion.features: Gain-of-function KCNJ2 (Kir2.1) variants such as V93I increase the inward-rectifier IK1 current and shorten atrial repolarization.

selected_evidence.snippet: Kir2.1 V93I mutation may play a role in initiating and/or maintaining AF by increasing the activity of the inward rectifier K(+) channel.

value.name: NUP155-related
value.description: Autosomal recessive familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in NUP155, encoding nucleoporin 155, a component of the nuclear pore complex important for nucleocytoplasmic transport and cardiac gene expression. Associated with a severe phenotype including sudden cardiac death in young individuals.

assertion.name: NUP155 biallelic loss-of-function variants
assertion.features: A homozygous R391H substitution in the nucleoporin NUP155 that cosegregates with AF in the family in which the 5p13 locus was mapped, mislocalizes the protein, and reduces nuclear envelope permeability.
assertion.notes: The only nuclear pore gene in this entry, and the one whose mechanism is furthest from ion flux: the reported defect is in nucleocytoplasmic transport, specifically of Hsp70 message and protein. It is also the strongest of the newer loci on human-plus-model evidence, since the heterozygous knockout mouse reproduces the AF phenotype even though the human variant is homozygous.

selected_evidence.snippet: The R391H mutation and reduction of NUP155 are associated with inhibition of both export of Hsp70 mRNA and nuclear import of Hsp70 protein.

value.name: MYL4-related
value.display_name: MYL4 (atrial myosin light chain) familial AF
value.description: Autosomal recessive familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in MYL4, encoding the atrial-specific essential myosin light chain. Associated with early-onset AF, atrial myopathy, and progressive atrial cardiomyopathy. Unlike the channelopathy subtypes, this one is a structural atrial disease, so the entry's framing of familial AF as arising in structurally normal hearts does not hold here.

assertion.name: MYL4 biallelic loss-of-function variant
assertion.features: A rare frameshift deletion, c.234delC, in the atrial-specific essential myosin light chain, fully penetrant for early-onset AF in the homozygous state.
assertion.notes:
MYL4 is the clearest demonstration in this entry that a monogenic AF gene need not be a channel: the product is the atrial-selective essential myosin light chain, and the phenotype is an atrial cardiomyopathy that includes sick sinus syndrome, stroke and sudden death alongside the arrhythmia. An independent family, reported separately, cosegregated a different MYL4 missense variant with atrial standstill, and knock-in and knockout rats reproduced the progressive electrical, contractile and fibrotic phenotype.
It is also the only locus here found by a population approach rather than by following a family, which is why the penetrance statement is unusually strong for this list. No case fraction is recorded: the study reports the allelic frequency and a homozygote count rather than a share of cases, and computing one from those two numbers would not be a reported figure.

selected_evidence.snippet: Three of the homozygotes had received pacemaker implantations due to sick sinus syndrome, three had suffered an ischemic stroke, and one suffered sudden cardiac death.

value.description: HSP caused by variants in REEP2 (previous symbol C5orf19, HGNC read 2026-09-25), a gene closely related to the SPG31 gene REEP1. value.name: CSS4
value.description:
The SMARCA4-related form of Coffin-Siris syndrome, corresponding to OMIM 614609. SMARCA4 encodes BRG1, the catalytic ATPase subunit of the BAF/PBAF chromatin-remodelling complex - so this is the subtype in which the motor of the complex is damaged rather than one of its scaffolding or targeting subunits.
The subtype carries two names for one concept, and the second name is the informative one. MONDO's primary label is "intellectual disability, autosomal dominant 16" (MRD16); its synonyms include "Coffin-Siris syndrome 4" and "SMARCA4-related BAFopathy"; and its definition is explicitly "any Coffin-Siris syndrome in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the SMARCA4 gene". The MRD16 label exists because a substantial fraction of SMARCA4 patients come to attention as non-syndromic intellectual disability or autism rather than as classic Coffin-Siris syndrome: in one series of eight children with novel SMARCA4 missense variants, all had moderate to severe intellectual disability and seven had autistic or likely-autistic features, while being *less* likely than published Coffin-Siris patients to show the craniofacial or finger and toe anomalies. Reading MRD16 as a separate disease from Coffin-Siris syndrome would split one gene's phenotypic range in two along an ascertainment line.
Genotype-phenotype, stated with the hedge the sources put on it. SMARCA4 variants in Coffin-Siris syndrome were originally all non-truncating - missense or in-frame deletion - which is the variant class this subtype was defined on, and which distinguishes it from the germline loss-of-function SMARCA4 alleles that cause rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome 2. That distinction has since softened: a 15-patient SMARCA4 registry cohort included two individuals with nonsense variants who had milder learning and behavioural differences and no organ-system involvement. At the level of gene families rather than individual alleles, SMARC-related Coffin-Siris patients have been proposed to have more severe organ-related complications than ARID-related patients - but the same study that reports that correlation concludes that everyone with a BAF-related condition is at risk of most of the phenotype and that surveillance should be broad. The correlation is a tendency, not a triage rule.
